system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel — Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Preliminary note on the Seller's preamble.** The preamble asserts the positions were "settled at principal level by both deal teams," are "FINAL" and "not intended to be re-opened," and are "market standard." None of this is supported by our record. Our playbook records **no** written authority from Amelia Frost for any fallback (20% cap, 18-month period or post-completion Riverlark release). Treat the preamble as advocacy, not as evidence of agreement; respond that all positions remain open and the Seller's "market" assertions do not substitute for a specific fallback approval. Also note the Disclosure Letter itself (para 11) disclaims any "negotiation position or approval" — which contradicts the preamble.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- *Seller:* 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- *Buyer wants:* 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** The 20% figure is our fallback only with prior written Amelia Frost authority identifying this draft, and none has been given.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- *Seller:* De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only recovery (cl 12.2).
- *Buyer wants:* De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar recovery once exceeded.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject on all three elements.** The Seller's thresholds are 5x ours and the "tipping" basket converts to a deductible, materially eroding recovery.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- *Seller:* 18 months; plus a sweep that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise (cl 12.3/13).
- *Buyer wants:* 24 months for general Warranty Claims; no catch-all override.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject; counter at 24 months and delete the "all Claims" sweep.** 18 months requires Amelia Frost written approval (none given), and the sweep would drag Fundamental/Tax/IP/indemnity claims into the general period.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- *Seller:* Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
- *Buyer wants:* Separate regime — 100% of price cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject outright.** A AUD 4.8m cap on title to the shares we are paying AUD 24m for is unacceptable regardless of other concessions.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- *Seller:* No fraud carve-out; cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance "to all Claims of any nature."
- *Buyer wants:* Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- *Recommendation:* **Insert a full carve-out; non-negotiable.** No member of the deal team has authority to waive this, and the Seller's "all Claims of any nature" wording purports to limit fraud.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- *Seller:* General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012 as at 22 Sept 2026), Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Sch 7; DL 1.1–1.2).
- *Buyer wants:* Specific fair disclosure only; no whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject DL 1.1/1.2 and Sch 7 general disclosure; require matter-by-matter fair disclosure against the specific warranty.** Blanket data-room disclosure would neutralise the warranties for matters buried in 11 folders. Also note DL 1.4 (no admission of consent, payment, etc. being required) should not be allowed to undercut the Bluefen, Riverlark and Ironquay specific obligations.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- *Seller:* No claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records" (cl 8.3).
- *Buyer wants:* Delete the blanket exclusion. Any qualifier must be limited to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry, and never apply to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- *Recommendation:* **Delete cl 8.3 entirely.** "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge standard that, combined with general disclosure, would eliminate warranty protection.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- *Seller:* Reasonable endeavours; condition "satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent" (cl 3/6.3). DL para 2 confirms no final written consent and no evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- *Buyer wants:* Effective consent **and** evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, as a Condition Precedent before Completion.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject; make effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) Bluefen consent a CP.** Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m); "consent on delivery" with unsatisfied conditions is no consent at all.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- *Seller:* ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion" (cl 2/7). DL para 3 confirms not repaid, no discharge.
- *Buyer wants:* Current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases delivered at Completion.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject post-completion release; require payout + release at Completion.** A post-completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable bank undertaking **and** Amelia Frost approval, neither of which exists; without it we buy a company still encumbered under the debt-free/cash-free price.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- *Seller:* DD-005 AUD 420,000 bonuses "a matter for the Seller," not itemised in the funds flow. DL para 5 confirms omission and is silent on payroll tax/super/on-costs.
- *Buyer wants:* AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or expressly Seller-funded.
- *Recommendation:* **Require a specific line item (bonuses + on-costs) or an express Seller-funding covenant/price adjustment.** Silence in the funds flow would leave the Company (i.e. the Buyer) bearing the cost post-Completion.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- *Seller:* Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate" (cl 11.1). DL para 4: DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on full payment; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; no receipt or assignment in data room.
- *Buyer wants:* Broadened indemnity covering non-transfer of IP, third-party claims and remediation costs, preserving the SOW3 cure (pay and obtain confirmatory assignment).
- *Recommendation:* **Broaden the indemnity; require cleared payment and confirmatory assignment pre-Completion or escrow the cure.** The AUD 180,000 is unverified either way, so the indemnity must cover the IP-ownership risk, not just the invoice.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- *Seller:* "Preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material (cl 4.6/Sch 6). DL para 6: ~1,240 records sent to an unintended external address; access, scope and notification duty undetermined.
- *Buyer wants:* Log preservation, completed investigation, update undertakings to Completion, and no general-disclosure of the incident against the privacy/data warranties.
- *Recommendation:* **Require investigation/preservation/update covenants and a specific indemnity for costs flowing from DD-006; do not accept "not material."** We assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or demand in either direction, so the position must be preserved rather than priced.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- *Seller:* Three renewals (AUD 330,000) are ordinary-course operating costs. DL para 8 does not state whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- *Buyer wants:* Assessment of timing, terminability and accrual (DD-008 + DD-011 read together); no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- *Recommendation:* **Hold position pending DD assessment; request the terms and any accrued liability.** The playbook does not mandate a price deduction, so don't claim one until the facts support it.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- *Seller:* Limitations apply to all Claims unless stated otherwise (cl 13); Tax/IP "settled under the general regime."
- *Buyer wants:* Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant claims kept in separate regimes with their own caps/periods; no hidden general-regime override.
- *Recommendation:* **Delete the general override and insert express carve-outs for each category.** The override is the mechanism by which SPA-N-003, -004 and -016 would be silently lost.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- *Seller:* Title evidenced by the DD-012 share register. DL para 10 concedes this is the source relied on and does not state the Buyer has verified.
- *Buyer wants:* Independent evidence — ASIC extract, constitution, board/share-transfer minutes, PPSR and encumbrance searches, signed authority and capacity evidence.
- *Recommendation:* **Require independent title/encumbrance/authority evidence as a CP.** DD-012 is a Seller-supplied internal document, not independent proof.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- *Seller:* Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime."
- *Buyer wants:* Tax and IP to remain open, negotiated separately, with their own cap and period.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject "settled"; record Tax/IP as OPEN.** Nothing has been agreed; we assume no unlimited liability and no resolution, so neither side should treat the general regime as applying.

---

**Summary for the deal team:** Of 16 issues, the Seller draft is adverse on 15 (Sandbar is neutral pending DD). Four items should be flagged as deal-critical: fraud carve-out (-005), Fundamental/Title regime (-004), Bluefen CP (-008) and Riverlark release at Completion (-009). Recommend the covering note to Seller counsel expressly reject the "FINAL / settled at principal level" characterisation and confirm no principal-level approvals have been given by Wattlebridge.
=== END ADVICE ===
